verdicts.note: The piece exists but not as queued: it is Bagatela 'S kyticí v ruce' ('With Nosegay in Hand'), 1917, publ. Hudební matice, Prague 1923 (H.M. 294), scored for flute, violin and piano (IMSLP also lists a 2 violins + piano alternative) - i.e. a chamber trio, not a violin solo/duo work. 'Bagatelle (1917)' is not a title in any source. If the owner still wants it, use title "Bagatelle 'S kyticí v ruce'", accompaniment '2 violins & piano', category 'Duet / Double Concerto', ~2 min, low level.

gaps.title: Melodie (arr. J. A. Suk)
gaps.scoring: violin and piano; simple arrangement by the composer's grandson, the violinist Josef Suk (b. 1929), of the early Melodie (1892/93; first for 2 violins, in the collection 'The Young Violinist')
gaps.edition: Editio Bärenreiter Praha H 7823 'Suk: Compositions for Violin & Piano' (new bowings/fingerings; earlier mostly Supraphon popular edition); also separate Bärenreiter 'Melody for 2 violins' H 7951
gaps.note: OPTIONAL (published and in print; I found no recording). 'Arr. J. A. Suk' = Josef Suk the violinist (1929-2011), not the composer; one listing mis-dates him 1924. Second source: Stretta Music listing of the same volume, https://www.stretta-music.pt/suk-compositions-for-violin-and-piano-nr-159853.html

gaps.title: Dumka (Elegie), Op. 7 No. 5 (arr. Ondříček)
gaps.scoring: violin and piano; arrangement by the violinist František Ondříček (1857-1922) of No. 5 of the 6 Piano Pieces, Op. 7
gaps.note: Same Op. 7 cycle as the existing Love Song (id 1282, arr. Kocián, Urbánek 1948 U. 2053). Recording not checked. Second source: Wikipedia's Suk work list only gives the Op. 7 piano cycle (no violin arrangements), so treat as IMSLP-only evidence.

existing_issues.issue: Arranger missing. IMSLP lists the violin & piano arrangement of Op. 7 No. 1 (Píseň lásky / Liebeslied / Love Song, from the 6 Piano Pieces, Op. 7) by Jaroslav Kocián, Urbánek, Prague 1948 (U. 2053); Bärenreiter H 7823 also prints Song of Love in Kocián's arrangement.

note: Gap check done against IMSLP (46 pages scanned), Wikipedia's work list and Bärenreiter. Not proposed because I found no published violin edition: Ballade in D minor for violin & piano (1890, recorded by Josef Suk on Supraphon; the published Op. 3 Ballade and Serenade is for cello), Polka in G major (1882), Minuet (1919?), Melodie for 2 violins in its original 1892 form. Fantasy Op. 24 and Four Pieces Op. 17 titles/numbers in the catalogue match IMSLP and Wikipedia.
